rows.author: I101;
rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING PLASTIC WASTE MANAGEMENT PROGRAMS AND MEASURES, PROHIBITING THE RELEASE OF PLASTIC WASTE INTO THE NATURAL ENVIRONMENT, EMPOWERING THE OMBUDSMAN TO IMPLEMENT WASTE MANAGEMENT LAWS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Identifies and prohibits certain acts that may cause damage to or death and destruction of animal and plant life and habitats; Imposes a plastic bags deterrence fee of at least twenty pesos (P20.00) per reusable bag for plastic use deterrence and discouragement purposes at point-of-sale transactions at all retail purchase outlets nationwide; Provides for the phase-out of single-use plastic and phase-in of non-toxic and food-safe reusable plastic for the packaging, presentation, and storage of food and beverages; Mandates DENR, DTI and DILG to jointly formulate, approve and implement a national policy and implementing rules on redemption, recovery and recycling of reusable plastic products and packaging.
rows.alias_name: “Plastic Waste Management and Prohibition Act of 2018.”
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECOLOGY since 2018-07-30

rows.author: D007;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE PHASE-OUT OF SINGLE-USE PLASTIC PRODUCTS IN THE COUNTRY AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Prohibits the sale and use of single-use of plastic products three years after the effectivity of this Act and thereafter, the production, manufacture and importation of such products shall no longer be allowed. Mandates different government agencies to formulate a Phase-Out Plan to carry out the objective of phasing out single-use plastic products in the country.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECOLOGY since 2018-07-30

rows.author: H061;
rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE PENALTY IMPOSED AGAINST POLLUTERS OF NAVIGABLE WATERS BY AMENDING SECTION 7 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 979 PROVIDING FOR THE REVISION OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 600 GOVERNING MARINE POLLUTION
rows.abstract: Imposes a fine of 5 million or imprisonment of 12 years or both to violators of this Act.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECOLOGY since 2018-07-30

rows.author: H061;
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING PLANTILLA POSITIONS IN THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION FOR VOLUNTEER TEACHERS WITH AT LEAST FIVE (5) YEARS OF CONTINUOUS SERVICE IN THE PUBLIC SCHOOL SYSTEM AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Recognizes the role of volunteer teachers in guiding the youth to become productive members of society by creating plantilla positions to accommodate them, if they have the appropriate qualifications.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2018-07-30

rows.author: H061;
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE SOLAR ENERGY DEVELOPMENT CENTER AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Aims to promote the use, research, and distribution of solar energy by creating a center for its utilization and development.
rows.status: Referred to Stakeholders on 2018-09-12

rows.author: H061;
rows.title_full: AN ACT INCORPORATING THE VALUE OF RESPONSIBLE, FAIR USAGE AND ENJOYMENT OF SOCIAL MEDIA IN CAMPUSES NATIONWIDE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Aims to educate children in using the internet in the efficient and effective dissemination of information, the importance of upholding truth and the veracity of facts, figures and events, and the responsible and fair use of Social Media.
rows.alias_name: “Social Media Awareness in Campuses Nationwide Act of 2018.”
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2018-07-30

rows.author: H061;
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING FUNERAL AND MEMORIAL DISCOUNT PRIVILEGES TO ALL PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS WHO DIED ON ACCOUNT OF WORK-RELATED SICKNESS AND INJURIES, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Provides 20% discount on funeral services and 10% discount on memorial lot to families of teachers who died on work-related sickness.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2018-07-30

rows.author: G110;G111;G109;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR VIDEO GAME CONTENT RATING AND CLASSIFICATION SYSTEM,AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Mandates the Gaming and Amusement Board (GAB) to rate and classify videogames into the following categories: “E” or For Everyone, “E10+” or “Everyone 10 years old or older”, “T” or “Teen”, “M” or “Mature”, “AO” or “Adults Only”,  “X” or Not Fit for Distribution”.
Declares it unlawful for any person to sell, lease, or distribute any video game or publicity material, including trailer, and stills in connection with such video games, without being rated and classified by the GAB.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC INFORMATION since 2018-07-30

rows.author: C005;C007;

rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE CATCHING SALE, PURCHASE, POSSESSION, TRANSPORTATION, IMPORTATION, AND EXPORTATION OF ALL SHARKS, RAYS, CHIMAERAS, OR ANY PART THEREOF IN THE COUNTRY
rows.abstract: Provides for the conservation and protection of sharks, management of their threats, and creation of shark sanctuaries. Declares the following acts as illegal and penalizes the same: killing, taking, keeping in captivity, inflicting injury, harassing and trading vulnerable, threatened, endangered, or critically endangered species, and finning  of sharks, among others.

rows.abstract: Aims to establish provincial and regional offices of the OWWA which would act as frontline offices for the OFWs in various regions.

rows.author: G084;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROMOTING NATIONAL ROAD SAFETY AWARENESS THROUGH ROAD SAFETY EDUCATION, ROAD SAFETY EVENTS AND ACTIVITIES AND MULTI-STAKEHOLDER CONSULTATION AND COLLABORATION, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Aims to address road crashes and deaths through safety education and awareness campaign and prevent road deaths and injuries, by providing for mandatory road safety education in school curricula at all levels. Declares the month of June as National Road Safety Month to stress the importance of road safety education. Mandates different government agencies to conduct nationwide information, education and communication campaigns on road safety laws, road crash data, risk factors, rights and responsibilities of all road users and all other matters which will help increase the awareness of the public on the importance of road safety.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION since 2018-07-30

rows.author: I097;
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING USED CAR DEALERS TO PROVIDE CONSUMERS WITH A WRITTEN WARRANTY AGAINST DEFECTS AND REQUIRING PRIVATE SELLERS TO DISCLOSE ANY KNOWN USE OR SAFETY DEFECTS
rows.abstract: Provides that no used car shall be sold by a dealer to a buyer unless given a warranty covering the full cost of parts and labor to repair the defect. It also provides the coverage of the warranty which will depend on the mileage of the vehicle at the time of its purchase or the if the true mileage is unknown, the warranty period shall be calculated according to the age of the vehicle.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2018-07-30

rows.author: I089;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING ALL TELECOMMUNICATIONS COMPANY (SERVICE PROVIDER) TO CHARGE AND COLLECT ADVANCE MONTHLY SERVICE FEES/MONTHLY RECURRING FEES/HANDSET COSTS FROM ALL SUBSCRIBERS AVAILING FOR A POSTPAID SUBSCRIPTION, TO PROMOTE CONSUMER PROTECTION UNDER ITS SERVICE CONTRACT, PROVIDING PENALTIES AND SANCTIONS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Aims to protect consumers of postpaid subscriptions  under a service contract by prohibiting telecom companies to charge advance monthly service fees, monthly recurring fees  and handset costs and penalizing such service providers for violation of this Act.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATIONS TECHNOLOGY since 2018-07-30

rows.author: G101;
rows.title_full: AN ACT FURTHER AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT 9501, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE \"MAGNA CARTA FOR MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES\" AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Provides that private mall and supermarkets shall provide at least 5 % of their selling area free of charge to qualified Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) to increase the access of MSMEs to the domestic market.
rows.status: Referred to the Technical Working Group (TWG) on 2018-09-25

first_reading.ref_name: MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISE DEVELOPMENT

committee_action.action: Referred to the Technical Working Group (TWG) on 2018-09-25
committee_action.remarks:
â€¢	Initial deliberation on the bill together with HB 8129 was conducted on September 25, 2018.
â€¢	A technical working group (TWG) was created to fine tune the provisions and craft the substitute bill to HBs Numbered 7918 and 8129.
committee_action.meethigh:
Rep. Carmelo Lazatin II sponsored the said bills on behalf of the authors.  The bills seek to further amend RA 9501 by  inserting a new provision requiring private malls and supermarkets to provide at least five percent (5%) or ten percent (10%) of their total selling area, free of charge to deserving MSMEs, to be identified by the Department of Trade and Industry. 

A Technical Working Group (TWG) was created to fine tune the provisions of the substitute bill to House Bills Numbered 7918 and 8129. The TWG Chair will still be determined.

In view thereof, HBs 7918 and 8129 will not be consolidated with HBs 4498 and 5540.

rows.abstract: Aims to raise people´s awareness on the causes,   consequences, and cost of road deaths and injuries by declaring 3rd Sunday of November a day of remembrance.

rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT TO INCREASE THE UNCONDITIONAL CASH TRANSFER (UCT) PROGRAM TO P500.00 TO BENEFIT 22 MILLION POOR FILIPINOS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Mandates the DSWD to increase the Unconditional Cash Transfer from P200 to P500 to promote poverty alleviation schemes in a successive and progressive manner.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2018-07-30

rows.author: I089;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING INCENTIVES AND MECHANISMS TO CREATE NEW JOBS AND OPPORTUNITIES, IMPROVE PRODUCTION, AND ADVANCE INNOVATION AND TRADE IN THE COUNTRY, TO FOSTER AND DEVELOP THE PHILIPPINE STARTUP ECOSYSTEM
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2018-07-30

rows.author: G020;
rows.title_full: AN ACT REDUCING WAIT TIME FOR REQUESTS FOR AN ACTION OR SERVICE IN PHONE CALLS FOR SERVICE-ORIENTED OFFICES AND PRESCRIBING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Prescribes a phone call protocol whereby callers shall be put on hold FOR NO MORE THAN TWO (2) MINUTES; Mandates the National Telecommunication Commission to issue the implementing rules and regulations.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2018-07-30

rows.author: D029;
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO STRENGTHEN DISCIPLINARY MECHANISM IN THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL POLICE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6975, AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8551, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Seeks to strengthen existing disciplinary mechanisms within the Philippine National Police (PNP) organization to overcome more challenging wars against sophisticated forms of criminality; Proposes to reconstitute the Internal Affairs Service (IAS) as “Internal Affairs” clothe with adjudicatory power to hear and decide, with finality, administrative cases filed against PNP uniformed members; 
Amends Sec.49 of R.A.8551 which grants IAS the power to “generally conduct summary proceedings and hearings” and, thus, only make disciplinary recommendations; Further proposes to establish a separate and distinct Police Justice System in cases of “breach of internal discipline” committed by uniformed members.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2018-07-30

rows.author: G118;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROMOTING SAFE AND RESPONSIBLE USE OF MODERN BIOTECHNOLOGY, ESTABLISHING THE BIOTECHNOLOGY AUTHORITY OF THE PHILIPPINES FOR THIS PURPOSE AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREOF
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY since 2018-07-30

rows.author: I088;I089;H057;F036;
rows.title_full: AN ACT INTEGRATING LABOR EDUCATION INTO THE SOCIAL SCIENCE SUBJECTS IN THE HIGHER EDUCATION CURRICULUM
rows.title_short: Integrating Labor Education Into The Social Science Subjects In The Higher Education Curriculum
rows.abstract: Aims to  educate the youth on the rights and welfare of the workers and promote a society that is responsive and sensitive to the needs of the labor sector by integrating Labor Education into the mandatory social science subjects being offered under the general education curriculum in the higher education courses.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2018-11-12, transmitted to the Senate on 2018-11-13 and received by the Senate on 2018-11-13

rows.author: H046;
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF COMPUTER LABORATORY IN ALL PUBLIC ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY SCHOOLS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Aims to give priority to promote the use of computer technology and literacy in basic education, especially in public schools;
Seeks to enhance and facilitate learning and education of pupils and students and provide access to computers and the Internet by both learners and teachers; Provides that every public elementary and high school students in the country shall have at least one (1) room that shall be used as computer laboratory.
rows.alias_name: “Computer and Internet Literacy for Public School Act”
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2018-07-30

rows.author: I094;
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A NATIONAL SPECIAL NEEDS SCREENING PROGRAM, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SOCIAL SERVICES since 2018-07-30

rows.author: I051;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR ADDITIONAL SUPPORT AND COMPENSATION FOR EDUCATORS IN BASIC EDUCATION
rows.abstract:
Proposes to give additional support in the form of allowances and other remuneration, medical allowance, and an annual Magna Carta Bonus in relation to the implementation of Republic 
Act 4670 (Magna Carta for Public School Teachers); Provides for the beneficiaries of the additional support and compensation in the amount of TEN THOUSAND (P10,000.00) per month which shall be paid in three (3) tranches and specifies the terms and conditions of its payment.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2018-07-30

rows.author: I051;
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING A COMPREHENSIVE HOUSING PROGRAM FOR PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Intends to help public school teachers to purchase a housing unit of their choice through loans with affordable interest and long-term repayment period; Seeks to engage the government housing and financing agencies (National Housing Authority, National Home Mortgage Finance Corporation, Home Guaranty Corporation, and the Government Service Insurance System) to spearhead the formulation and the implementation of the proposed program of this Act; Proposes further the provision of on-site living quarters, free of charge, for public school teachers in remote and hard-to-reach areas.
rows.status: Referred to the Subcommittee on 2018-08-29

committee_action.remarks: -Subcommittee on Housing for the Low-Income and Marginalized Sector

rows.author: I051;
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A COMPETITIVE GRANT PROGRAM TO RETAIN HIGHLY QUALIFIED TEACHERS IN RURAL COMMUNITIES
rows.abstract: Explains the term “child with disability” as a minor who has a physical, mental or medical impairment resulting from an anatomical, physiological, or neurological condition that prevents the exercise of a normal bodily function or that substantially impair cognitive function, and include but is not limited to impairments requiring the use of an artificial device; Seeks to counter massive migration of top Filipino teachers who leave the country by providing financial incentive to these highly qualified teachers or highly qualified special education teachers in rural areas; Provides therefore a five-year pilot program; and tasks the DepEd to award grants to not more than ten (10) provinces to enable them to extend salary bonuses to above-mentioned teachers who will teach, or will commit to teach, for at least three (3) academic years in select rural academic institutions.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2018-07-30

rows.author: I051;
rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE CONTINUITY OF EDUCATIONAL CURRICULUM FOR A PERIOD OF AT LEAST SIX (6) YEARS AND ENSURING THE STABILITY OF THE CONSEQUENT TEXTBOOKS AND RELATED MATERIALS THROUGH AN ANNUAL REVIEW, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8047, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE BOOK PUBLISHING INDUSTRY ACT, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract:
Amends Republic Act No. 8047 (Book Publishing Industry Act) to improve competencies of educational materials in public schools by mandating that curriculum should have continuity and stability by keeping the same for a period of at least SIX (6) years;
Intends to resolve errors in textbooks and related materials and to ensure that they are up to standards by conducting ANNUAL review by the DepEd in cooperation with National Book Development Board.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2018-07-30

rows.author: I051;
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING A FIVE PERCENT (5%) BUDGETARY ALLOCATION OF BARANGAYS FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROGRAMS, PROJECTS, ACTIVITIES, AND SERVICES FOR SENIOR CITIZENS, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE THE PERTINENT PROVISIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE \"LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE\" AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Proposes to authorize the allocation of five percent (5%) of the total internal revenue allotment for barangays for the welfare of senior citizens and to provide financial aid to those indigent elderly in need.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2018-07-30

rows.author: I051;
rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING ELECTRONIC CIGARETTES
rows.abstract: Intends to require producers of E-cigarette products to follow the product standard requirements in order to register them with the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) to ensure conformity to quality and safety standards; Proposes to prohibit the sale and distribution of said products to persons below EIGHTEEN (18) years old and provides that only nicotine containers shall bear textual health warnings “This product may damage your health and is addictive”.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2018-09-11

rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2018-07-30

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE COMMISSION ON IMMIGRATION, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, EXPANDING, RATIONALIZING AND FURTHER PROFESSIONALIZING ITS ORGANIZATION, UPGRADING THE COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS OF ITS OFFICIALS AND EMPLOYEES, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.title_short: Creating The Commission On Immigration, Defining Its Powers And Functions, Expanding, Rationalizing And Further Professionalizing Its Organization, Upgrading The Compensation And Benefits Of Its Officials And Employees
rows.abstract: Seeks to create the Commission on Immigration which shall be under the control and supervision of the Department of Justice (DOJ). The Commission shall be responsible in the implementation of all laws, rules, regulations or orders of any competent authority concerning the entry and admission into, stay in, and the departure from the Philippines of all persons.
rows.status: Pending With Rules (Included in OB on 2018-07-30)

first_reading.recomm: Recommending its approval in substitution of House Bills Numbered 162, 327, 435, 1305, 1697 and 3005

rows.author: H061;
rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE USE OF GOVERNMENT AMBULANCES, PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFORE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Seeks to address the many problems that beset emergency medical response in the country particularly the appropriate utilization of ambulance/s in local government.  Provides that such government ambulance/s donated or acquired by an LGU shall be under the joint custody of the local chief executive and the health officer concerned.  
Identifies the duties of the Local Chief Executives and the prohibited acts as regards the use of said vehicles and provides that they be allowed to be used in non-emergency cases only during medical outreach missions and other related hospital operations.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2018-08-01

rows.author: H061;
rows.title_full: AN ACT RECOGNIZING NATIONAL SCENIC BYWAYS IN THE PHILIPPINES, CREATING A NATIONAL SCENIC BYWAYS PROGRAM, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Defines among others, “Byway” as a minor or secondary road or a road other than the main road; and “National Scenic Byway” as a road that is recognized for its outstanding scenic, historic, natural, recreational, and archaeological qualities.
Intends to preserve and protect such roads in the country alongside the promotion of tourism and economic development through infrastructural improvement such as centers, overlooks, and rest areas. 
Provides for “Corridor Management Plan” developed by the community/communities along a scenic byway which outlines the mechanisms for the protection and enhancement of the byways´ intrinsic qualities and character that define the byway corridor.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC WORKS AND HIGHWAYS since 2018-08-01

rows.author: H061;
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING SUSTAINABLE COASTAL TOURISM, PROVIDING MECHANISMS FOR ITS INSTITUTIONALIZATION, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Proposes to ensure the continued rise and longevity of our tourism industry through conservation, protection, and strengthening of our natural resources. Specifically addresses urgent issues on development planning and mitigation efforts on our coastal resources, creating therefore the National Coastal Recreational Area Quality Framework which will form and implement tourism development measures and practices which shall include among others, measurable and reasonable quality standards requirements such as ecological waste management; water quality and sanitation; protection of marine flora and fauna, etc.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TOURISM since 2018-08-01

rows.author: H061;
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO EXPAND THE COVERAGE OF MICRO ENTERPRISES AS BENEFICIARIES OF THE MAGNA CARTA FOR MICRO, SMALL, AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES OR REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6977, AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8289 AND FURTHER AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9501
rows.abstract:
Amends existing laws on Magna Carta for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises specifically MSMEs categories based on total assets in order to ensure that more businesses are qualified to enjoy the benefits of specialized programs for the said sector.  Provides that Sec.3 of Republic Act No. 6977, as amended by Republic Act Nos. 8289 and  9501, is hereby amended to read as follows:  MSMEs shall be defined as any business activity or enterprise engaged in industry, agribusiness, and/or services ”¦ whose total assets ”¦ must have value falling under the following categories:
Micro:  not more than [3,000,000] P7,500,000
Small:  [P3,000,001 - P15,000,000] P7,500,001 - P15,000,000
Medium: [P15,000,001 - P100,000,000] P15,000,001 - P100,000,000.
rows.status: Tabled by the Committee on 2018-10-10

first_reading.ref_name: MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISE DEVELOPMENT

committee_action.action: Deliberated upon by the Mother Committee on 2018-09-19
committee_action.meethigh:
Rep. Teodoro Montoro sponsored the said bill on behalf of the author. The bill intends to amend the definition of micro and small enterprises, as follows:
â€¢	micro	-   from an asset size of not more than P3 Million, to an asset size of not more 	 	    	    than P7.5 Million
â€¢	small	-  from an asset size of P3,000,001-P15 Million, to an asset size of P7,500,001- P15 Million

Majority of the agencies, namely, the Department of Trade and Industry, Department of Science and Technology, Department of Agriculture, Department of Finance, Small Business Corporation, Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, and Philippine Exporters Confederation (PHILEXPORT) want to retain the current definition of MSMEs. 

Only Ka-Entrep Micro and Small Organization of the Philippines welcomed the proposal to amend the definition.

In view thereof, HB 7943 will not be consolidated with HBs 4498 and 5540.

rows.author: H061;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE PROTECTION AND CONSERVATION OF UNDERWATER CULTURAL HERITAGE IN PHILIPPINE WATERS
rows.abstract:
Intends to supplement existing laws as regards to “cultural properties” under R.A. No.4846 (Cultural Properties Preservation and Protection Act); P.D. No.374 (Amends R.A. No.4846); R.A.No.8492 (National Museum Act); and R.A. No.10066 (National Cultural Heritage Act).
Aims therefore to establish comprehensive underwater cultural heritage preservation, protection, management, and monitoring mechanism by creating regulatory framework particularly:  regulations on excavation and exploration, the creation of a registry of items and/or sites to be protected, prohibition of certain harmful activities, a reward system for verified reports and imposition of sanction/penalties for violations.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2018-08-01

rows.author: H056;
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROTECT MARINE MAMMALS AND ENSURE THEIR SURVIVAL FOR THE BENEFIT OF FUTURE GENERATIONS
rows.abstract:
Seeks to address “data deficient” status of the populations of most marine mammals in the country so that they can be evaluated and identified whether critically endangered, endangered, and vulnerable.
Intends to encourage and support research of wildlife populations by partnering with local community organizations, academic and scientific institutions in order to form a database that will support conservation programs.
Creates the Marine Protected Areas and Networks and Marine Corridors that shall seek to protect wild populations from heavy industries; and the Marine Mammal Protection and Conservation Committee (MMPCC) tasks with functions related to research programs; rescue of stranded animals; dolphin and whale-watching tours; rescued, stranded or rehabilitated marine mammals, etc.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 2018-08-01

rows.author: H056;
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING RESTAURANTS AND OTHER SIMILAR FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS TO DISCLOSE AND DISPLAY NUTRITIONAL INFORMATION OF FOOD AND BEVERAGES ON THEIR MENUS AND MENU BOARDS
rows.abstract:
Aims to help Filipinos make an informed and healthier decision on their food choices by providing that food establishments disclose the corresponding nutrient content, in a clear and conspicuous manner as regard to:  total calories; calories from fat; total fat; saturated fat; trans fat; cholesterol; Sodium; total carbohydrates; dietary fiber; sugars; and protein
Provides that the statement:  “2,000 calories a day is used for general nutrition advice, but calorie needs vary” be posted prominently to enable consumers to understand, in the context of a total daily diet, the significance of calorie information.
Also includes provision for menus and menu boards targeting children with options as a substitute for or in addition to the above statement.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2018-08-01

rows.author: I105;
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROVIDE FOR A STUDY AND FOR DEMONSTRATION PROJECTS REGARDING CASES OF HEPATITIS C AMONG FIREFIGHTERS, PARAMEDICS, EMERGENCY MEDICAL TECHNICIANS AND OTHER EMERGENCY RESPONSE EMPLOYEES
rows.abstract:
Intends to provide programs to prevent emergency response employees from acquiring Hepatitis C (a viral infection that causes liver inflammation, sometimes leading to serious liver damage).
Seeks to establish a system, training, protocol and scientific research and medical treatment for this virus so that our said personnel will be able to deploy their functions without sacrificing their precious health.

rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING ELECTRONIC CIGARETTES
rows.abstract:
Defines among others:  “E-cigarette” (product that can be used for the consumption of a nicotine-containing vapour) “Nicotine” (nicotinic alkaloids, including any salt or complex of nicotine whether derived from tobacco or synthetically produced); “Vaping” (act of using an e-cigarette).
Provides that nicotine containers shall bear a textual health warnings “This product may damage your health and is addictive”; and a retailer signage statement shall likewise be posted:  “SALE/DISTRIBUTION TO OR PURCHASE BY MINORS OF E-CIGARETTES IS UNLAWFUL” or “IT IS UNLAWFUL FOR E-CIGARETTES TO BE SOLD/DISTRIBUTED TO OR PURCHASED BY PERSONS UNDER 18 YEARS OF AGE”.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2018-08-08

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING CHAPTER VII TITLE VI AND SECTION 151, AND CREATING NEW SECTIONS 151-A AND 151-B, OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8424, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE CODE OF 1997, AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Proposes to resolve the complex and differentiated fiscal regime currently accorded to mining sector through a rationalized and a single fiscal regime applicable to all mineral agreements and FTAA (Financial and Technical Assistance Agreement) to promote fairness.
Further proposes to: retain the royalty rate of five percent (5%) for those currently located inside a mineral reservation, and a phased-in-rate for those outside such reservation; to retain the imposition of the corporate income tax (CIT); to impose an additional government share when the basic share is less than fifty percent (50%) of the net mining revenue.
Introduces thin capitalization in order for the businesses not to depend on excessive debt funding; and ring-fencing per project to prevent consolidation of income and expenses of all mining projects by the same taxpayer.
rows.status: Substituted by HB08400

rows.author: I105;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING HEALTH MAINTENANCE ORGANIZATION (HMO) FOR ALL PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS
rows.abstract:
Recognizes the teacher´s role in educating and shaping the youth by compensating them not just with monetary remuneration but also with medical healthcare.
Provides therefore a health maintenance organization (HMO) program for all public school teachers in all levels in order to promote and maintain their health.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2018-08-08

rows.author: I105;
rows.title_full: AN ACT FURTHER AMENDING SECTIONS 101 (A)(I) AND SECTION 169 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 612, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS \"THE INSURANCE CODE\", AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10607
rows.abstract:
Seeks to address contingencies arising from terrorist and rebellious activities which exposes our countrymen to wide forms of risks involving death, destruction of property, stoppage of livelihood among others.
Amends R.A. No.10607 as amended, to read as follows:
“SEC.169. . . . the term fire insurance shall include insurance against loss by fire, lightning, windstorm, tornado or earthquake, ACTS OF REBELLION OR TERRORISM and other allied risks, when such risks are covered by extension to fire insurance policies or under separate policies.”
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BANKS AND FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARIES since 2018-08-08
